The depth of grooves increased with the increase of laser power and scanning times,because Cu was continuously excited under energy input, and the measurements of the groove depth are presented in Table I.

The shape of the laser-scanned groove was similar to a"V"character sincethefocusedlaser wasa Gaussianbeam,andthe intensity cross-sectional profile of a Gaussian beam at any position on the optical axis is Gaussian. Therefore, the property ofthe Gaussian beam at the center point had the greatest light intensity,which caused the center of the laser beam to be more effective in removing materials than the surrounding areas.
The microscopic morphology of the surface pickled microstructure is shown in Fig. 3. The surface of Cu presented regular laser-constructed grooves on the surface. These grooves

significantly increased the surface area, and surfaces with different groove spacings can be obtained by adjusting the interval of the laser scanning. The smaller the spacing of the grooves,the more surface area was increased. The grooves were filled with ultrafast laser-excited nanoparticles, which could significantly improve the surface energy of the grooves. The formation of the sintered neck required energy,and nanoparticles with high surface energy on thesubstrate couldforma better connectionwith Ag_NPsto improve the connection strength of the interface. The nanoparticles were stable on the substrate surface even after ultrasonic pickling.
